page-open-access-meta-description: No single company controls who can use Ethereum. Learn how censorship resistance gives you open access to hold ETH, send transactions, publish and build.
page-open-access-hero-description-1: A bank can freeze your account. A payment company can block your transfer. Nobody can block an Ethereum transaction.
page-open-access-hero-description-2: No single company controls who can use the network. If you have internet, you can hold and send ETH worldwide, use apps, or build your own.
page-open-access-summary-item-1: Open to anyone. Vital services like a bank account should be available to all.
page-open-access-summary-item-2: No single company controls Ethereum. The network is run by independent participants around the world, making it harder to shut down.
page-open-access-summary-item-3: No one can freeze your ETH. There is no company or central authority that can block a specific owner from using it.
page-open-access-summary-item-4: It is about neutral infrastructure, not a lack of rules. Apps and businesses built on Ethereum can still moderate their services and follow local laws.
page-open-access-frozen-title: Imagine your bank account frozen overnight
page-open-access-frozen-description-1: You wake up and see a strange notification. Your account has been frozen. Your money is still there, but you cannot spend it, transfer it, or pay your bills.
page-open-access-frozen-description-2: Most of us rarely think about who controls our digital access until something goes wrong. This still happens today. In 2025, US regulators reported that people had their accounts frozen or suddenly closed, sometimes leaving them unable to access their money for long periods.
page-open-access-frozen-description-3: Sometimes restrictions have a good reason. Sometimes they result from fraud detection, verification problems or mistakes. The important point is that when your money depends on one provider, that provider has the ability to restrict your access.
page-open-access-frozen-description-4: And many people never get access in the first place. According to the latest World Bank Global Findex, 1.3 billion adults worldwide still do not have a financial account. Around 900 million of them have a mobile phone.
page-open-access-frozen-description-5: Ethereum does not replace banks or solve every cause of financial exclusion, but it offers an alternative financial network that does not require permission from a central operator.
page-open-access-frozen-image-alt: An Ethereum logo locked inside a vault.
page-open-access-freedom-lead: Financial freedom means having meaningful control over your money and the choices you make with it.
page-open-access-freedom-description-1: It is often associated with having enough income or savings to live independently. But access matters too. Money is much less useful if you cannot reach it or move it when you need to.
page-open-access-freedom-description-2: Ethereum offers the ability to hold and transfer ETH without depending on a company to keep your account open.
page-open-access-censorship-resistance-d: Censorship resistance is a system's ability to remain usable even when someone tries to block a user or transaction.

On Ethereum, no single company, validator or app operator controls access to the main network. A particular service may refuse a transaction, but that service does not get the final say for Ethereum as a whole.
This is the technical property behind Ethereum's open access.
page-open-access-property-permissionless: You do not need to apply for an Ethereum account.
There is no central signup process, identity check or administrator who must approve you before you can interact with the network.
page-open-access-property-neutral-descri: The Ethereum protocol applies the same rules to everyone.
The network checks whether a transaction follows its rules, not whether it agrees with who sent it or why.
page-open-access-property-no-off-switch-: Ethereum does not run from one company's servers.
Independent computers called nodes operate the network around the world. Removing one node, company or service does not shut Ethereum down.
page-open-access-property-shared-record-: Once transactions have been confirmed by the network, there is no administrator who can quietly edit the database or delete inconvenient history.
Changing Ethereum's shared record requires agreement under the network's consensus rules.
page-open-access-alternative-description: Most people will continue using banks, websites and other intermediaries because they are convenient and useful.
Censorship resistant infrastructure provides another option when those systems become unavailable, unreliable or hostile.
You may rarely need that option, but its value becomes clearer on the day you do.
page-open-access-emergency-description-1: When Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, the country introduced emergency limits on cash withdrawals and some financial transfers to protect the banking system. At the same time, Ukraine published official crypto addresses, including an Ethereum address, so people around the world could send funds directly.
page-open-access-emergency-description-2: Within the first 100 days, the official Aid for Ukraine crypto fund had received more than $60 million in cryptoassets.
page-open-access-emergency-description-3: Crypto did not replace Ukraine's banks. It provided another way to move value when speed, borders and access mattered.
page-open-access-emergency-description-4: That is the value of censorship resistant infrastructure: another path when the systems you normally rely on become restricted, unavailable or unreliable.
page-open-access-participate-description: You can hold assets and send transactions without needing an institution to continuously approve your participation.
This can matter when services leave a country, or when access to traditional financial infrastructure is limited.
page-open-access-publish-description-1: Information stored through decentralized systems can be much harder for one organization to quietly remove or rewrite.
page-open-access-publish-description-2: This does not make every form of publishing permanent or appropriate. It means no single hosting company needs to be the final authority over what can exist.
page-open-access-build-description-1: Developers can deploy programs to Ethereum without asking Ethereum for an API key, developer account or app store approval.
page-open-access-build-description-2: Once deployed, those programs do not depend on one company's continued permission to exist.
page-open-access-how-description-1: Ethereum spreads control across many independent participants. Anyone can run a node and independently check the network's rules. Validators across the world propose and confirm blocks of transactions. Multiple independent teams build the software used to operate the network.
page-open-access-how-description-2: There is no Ethereum headquarters that can be ordered to switch the network off, and there is no central Ethereum account system that can suspend a user.
page-open-access-how-description-3: This makes sustained censorship much harder to coordinate because it requires controlling or influencing many independent parts of the system rather than one administrator.
page-open-access-how-description-4: A validator or block builder can leave a transaction out of a block. But another participant can include it in a later block. A transaction can be delayed but never fully stopped.
page-open-access-eth-title: ETH is not like other crypto assets
page-open-access-eth-description-1: Many crypto assets are issued by companies that keep some control over them. For example, issuers of stablecoins such as USDC and USDT can block addresses and freeze tokens when required.
page-open-access-eth-description-2: ETH works differently. It is the native asset of Ethereum, not a token issued by a company or controlled by a smart contract. There is no administrator key that can freeze the ETH in a particular account.
page-open-access-eth-description-3: If you control your account and can access the Ethereum network, no single company can revoke your ability to use your ETH.
page-open-access-started-description: You do not need to become an expert to reduce how much your digital access depends on intermediaries. An easy first step is to try and install a crypto wallet. These are free applications for your phone or desktop that can get you started with Ethereum.
page-open-access-wallet-callout-descript: A wallet gives you direct control over the keys to your Ethereum account rather than asking a company to hold them for you.
page-open-access-beyond-description-1: Ethereum is only one part of a much larger effort to keep digital infrastructure open.
page-open-access-beyond-description-2: Organizations around the world work on internet access, free expression, resilient communication, privacy and access to information.
page-open-access-org-eff-description: Defends digital civil liberties in the courts and in public policy
page-open-access-org-access-now-descript: Works to defend digital rights and documents internet shutdowns worldwide.
page-open-access-org-internet-archive-de: Preserves the web and defends the right to read, lend, and archive online
page-open-access-org-tor-description: Builds open anonymity and anti-censorship tools
page-open-access-org-freedom-press-descr: Develops tools and resources that support journalists and press freedom.
page-open-access-org-rsf-description: Works to protect freedom of information and journalists around the world.
page-open-access-future-description-1: Digital systems do not have to be built around permanent permission from a handful of gatekeepers.
page-open-access-future-description-2: We can build infrastructure where companies still provide useful services, communities still set their own rules, and laws still apply, while no single intermediary holds the final switch over everyone's access.
page-open-access-future-description-3: That is the promise of censorship resistance.
page-open-access-future-description-4: And it is one of the principles Ethereum is designed to protect.
